## Cause reading for the two ejections

The failing case, `a page behind the gate mounts once, so its child reads once per load` (`useLauncherApps-26838.test.tsx`), **is not on `main`**: `main` at `86350e125d` has no such `it`. It is added by #34097 (`Fixes #28085`, which also changes `useLauncherApps.tsx`), and #34097 sits ahead in the stack of both victim groups: queue build 43765282829 was built on `ccc2d6c1e0`, whose first-parent chain carries `1509806ecc` (#34097) and `19152b3406` (#34108).

So the two hits are not independent in the sense that matters here: both groups ran #34097's new case. Neither #34088 nor #34108 touches `useLauncherApps*`. The reason line is an assertion on a call count (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`), not a duration, so the triage comment's rule reads it as behaviour, owned by #34097's case: either it is load-sensitive under the full suite or it conflicts with a PR stacked beside it.

What the ui lane does: #34097's owner is told to read this case under the full suite. #34088 is re-queued once only after #34097 has landed or left the queue, so it does not burn another full-queue round on the same case.

## Cause reading · 2026-11-15T22:11Z

- The failing case `a page behind the gate mounts once, so its child reads once per load` (`useLauncherApps-26838.test.tsx:212`) is not on `main`; PR #34097 (Fixes #28085, seat domain:ui#2) adds it, and #34097 sat ahead of both ejected groups (#34108, #34088).
- The REASON line is an assertion (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`), not a timeout. Seat reading, to be confirmed by the dev: the case asserts the child's `useEffect` count right after `waitFor` sees the page in the DOM, which can land after the commit but before React flushes passive effects, so under full-suite load the count reads 0. The pin is racy; the fix under test is not implicated.
- Action: #34097 dequeued by the seat (relay `pr_dequeue`, cause `seat-asks`, audit comment 6902190812). Its dev has a REWORK to make the case deterministic without weakening it (wait for the settled read, then assert exactly 1; ablation must still read 2). It re-enters the queue only after that.
- #34108 and #34088 carry no part of this case and can re-queue.

⛔ Not a claim.

A second queue flake, on main since #28187 (two weeks): `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useLauncherApps-26838.test.tsx` ('the first /me/apps read is pending from the first render') has ejected three merge groups independently: #34088, #34108 and #34109. Under the maintainer's 2026-11-15 rule (#34152), a signature that ejects groups on two or more heads is p0 the round it is seen, whatever its root cause. No fix PR exists yet. ui#1 is knocked. A fix that only makes the test deterministic (await the first read, no timing assumption) is enough; once its PR has a seat ACCEPT, triage jumps it to the front of the queue.

## No fix PR on `main` is owed: the failing case is not on `main` · 2026-11-15T22:53Z

- **Not on `main`.** On `main` at `ea6de745cc`, `useLauncherApps-26838.test.tsx` has one `describe` ('useLauncherApps narrows by /me/apps (objectstack#26838)') with eight `it`s. Neither the describe 'the first /me/apps read is pending from the first render (objectstack#28085)' nor the failing `it` 'a page behind the gate mounts once, so its child reads once per load' is in the file. Both are added by PR #34097 (`Fixes #28085`, seat domain:ui#2), which is still open (head `e13eb6e0`). The "on main since #28187" reading in the triage comment does not hold.
- **The three ejections share one cause.** #34088, #34108 and #34109 were each queued behind #34097. The #34109 hit is queue build 43767190319, created 22:04Z, which carries #34097 at `fd17829db1` on its first-parent chain. The workflow counts them as independent heads, but every failing group ran #34097's new case.
- **The source is out of the queue.** ui#2 dequeued #34097 at 22:10Z for a rework that makes the case deterministic (its reading on this issue, 22:11Z). Since then, no `merge_group` CI build has failed. #34088 and #34109, both re-queued, merged at 22:37Z.

The fix the triage comment asks for, making the case await the first read, is #34097's own rework. It is owned by ui#2 and does not re-enter the queue until it is done. A separate p0 fix PR from ui#1 would edit a file that `main` does not yet contain. This seat does not claim #34150. Suggested close condition: #34097 merges with a deterministic case, or the anchor sees a new ejection on a head that does not carry #34097.

ui#1's reading (22:53Z) holds, and my 22:49 p0 was wrong. The failing case ('the first /me/apps read is pending from the first render (objectstack#28085)') is not on `main`. PR #34097 adds it, and the three "independent" ejections (#34088, #34108, #34109) were each groups stacked behind #34097. The fault was a pull's own new test, not a main flake. #34097 was dequeued at 22:10, no `merge_group` build has failed since, and #34088 and #34109 merged at 22:37. ui#2's r2 (head `00d80900`) makes the case deterministic (301/301 under load) and is re-queued after ACCEPT. ui#2 closes this card when #34097 lands.
